summary: Give a character's identity one owner: the pack carries the authored record and the simulation reads it, replacing the hard-coded hero literals the code itself marked provisional

coordination.notes: This is the first contract in this run that is not content-only, and it closes a defect the code had flagged against itself. world.rs:3455 carried the comment 'Provisional: the manifest reserves no field for the captain's name or history, so the scenario's hero identity stays here', and hard-coded display_name Michael, sex male, age 20 and a backstory string -- while content/characters/captain.json described the same person independently. They had already diverged: the record's displayName is 'Michael Corrigan' with metadata.titleCardName 'Michael'. One fact, two owners, which AGENTS.md rule 4 forbids. The character schema gains an explicit island block (boardName, sex, age, backstory) rather than the simulation guessing which of displayName/titleCardName the board should show; the pack gains a characters key resolved by the same array-of-paths mechanism triggers/quests/resources already use; from_scenario reads the record and refuses (scenario_captain_record_missing) a pack that starts a captain it does not carry, instead of substituting a default. The simulation deliberately deserialises only the island block -- art, skills and provenance belong to the presentation and battle owners, and copying them into the simulation would create a second copy to rot. Motivation beyond hygiene: this is the precondition for Betty. personas.json is a PROCEDURAL pool (given names, family names, histories per actor definition), so putting an authored individual there would generate a random woman named Betty rather than the authored one; there was no mechanism at all for placing a named authored character until this.
